title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: STANDING ACTIONS FIRST — four items have now survived three fires with zero movement, and one of them expires tomorrow (MCP Live!, Sep 9, 16:00–20:00 UTC)
bullets.summary: Not news; this report's own open decisions, listed first per the rule the 10:05 fire closed with. (a) Misalignment incident log — still not opened; two questions per entry: what did an agent touch that we did not authorise, and what would we have had to be watching to see it. (b) Entra's four MCP controls copied into a config script — discover shadow servers, allow/block per tool, pin protocol version, pin transport; three of the four need nothing but a script that reads our own config. (c) /skill-doctor against the ~130-skill corpus — shipped Sep 4, named on three fires, still not run. (d) MCP Live! — TOMORROW, Sep 9, 16:00–20:00 UTC, a half-day livestream covering enterprise MCP authentication, governance and security; the only standing item with a hard date, and therefore the only one that expires rather than merely ages.
bullets.how: YES. An item that survives three fires is not a to-do, it is a decision the report makes silently every morning and refuses to write down. Bullets 2 and 3 are what that decision cost this week, in kind rather than in days.

bullets.title: THE COVERAGE FAILURE, INSTANCE ONE — AIR came out of stealth on Sep 1 with $50M to build a firewall for AI agents that VETS THE SKILLS AND ADD-ONS AGENTS USE, and reports it filters out ~27% of the agent skills it evaluates. This report has never carried it, on any fire, in eight days
bullets.summary: Sequoia led an initial $10M seed, Greenoaks led a further $40M; founders Yair Saban (CEO) and Niv Hoffman (CTO), both Unit 8200 veterans; 20+ enterprise customers concentrated in financial services and pharmaceuticals, per SecurityWeek's independent write-up of the same launch. The product discovers agents running inside a company, continuously vets the skills, tools and MCP servers those agents consume, blocks the ones that fail its criteria, and operates a marketplace of pre-vetted add-ons. The 27% filter rate is the company's own figure for the public add-on and skill population it evaluates, and should be read as an order-of-magnitude prior rather than a measurement of anyone's specific corpus.
bullets.how: YES, and the most directly aimed item this report has carried in a week. The Construct runs roughly 130 skills and about 20 OAuth-connected MCP servers, none of which has ever been vetted by anything except our own judgement at install time. A quarter of a public skill population failing a security screen is the number that turns standing action (c) from tidy to urgent. Note the sequencing nobody should have needed to point out: on Sep 1 the market funded skill-vetting at $50M, on Sep 4 Anthropic shipped us a free skill diagnostic, and we have run neither.

bullets.title: THE COVERAGE FAILURE, INSTANCE TWO — Yodeck (65,000+ customers) launched an MCP-based AI Agent for digital signage management on Sep 1; this report carried the CastHub / Screenly / Revel Digital signage-MCP matrix on five separate fires in August and never once picked up the largest vendor's own launch
bullets.summary: Built on open MCP. Drives ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf and the Claude Code CLI. It can read, create, update and manage supported content across screens, media, playlists, schedules, workspaces, users and roles, with the vendor's own framing that tasks which used to take ten minutes now take ten seconds. Announced by press release on September 1 and picked up the same week by the signage trade press.
bullets.how: YES. This is Brand 9's trade, and it is the second item in four days — after the 60,000-detail Signage Details corpus — showing that the signage industry's agentic layer is being built by software vendors while this report reads the AI industry instead. The concrete read is a repositioning, not an alarm: the addressable operator wedge in signage is no longer 'manage the screens,' because Yodeck now does that free inside Claude. It is the design, permitting, fabrication and installation knowledge that no CMS holds and no CMS is buying.

bullets.title: THE ENTERPRISE-SECURITY WAVE IS ARRIVING AS PRODUCTS, NOT PAPERS — CrowdStrike opened an AI Partner Specialization framed around 'the agentic enterprise' and Proofpoint put a SOC Analyst Agent into private preview, GA expected end of Q3, that turns natural-language questions into traceable investigation findings
bullets.summary: Read alongside the Entra MCP Firewall carried on the first fire and AIR in bullet 2, that is four vendors in roughly one week selling agent governance as a purchasable product rather than as advice. SOURCE QUALITY STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: this bullet rests on a secondary aggregation of early-September enterprise announcements, not on four primaries read individually, and is tagged accordingly.
bullets.how: MAYBE. None of these is a purchase for us. What it is good for is pricing: the governance layer PRAGMA sells as expertise is being commoditised into SKUs on a timescale of weeks, and the word 'traceable' in Proofpoint's framing is the same word our whole attribution story rests on. When the differentiator becomes a checkbox on someone's partner program, the remaining defensible half is the operator judgement about what to point at what.

bullets.title: arXiv, the beat this report keeps sampling rather than reading — 'Agentic Context Management' (2607.21503) argues naive context accumulation grows token cost QUADRATICALLY in conversation length, while only VALIDATED compaction achieves linear cost with preserved fidelity
bullets.summary: The paper's move is to refuse to treat agent memory and agent cost as two separate engineering problems, framing both as one lifecycle-and-architecture question — the same structural claim as the ACE generate-reflect-curate loop carried at 10:05, whose delete-half this report has already flagged as the part our self-improving loop omits. The word doing the work is VALIDATED: compaction that is not checked for fidelity buys the linear cost curve by silently discarding the thing you needed.
bullets.how: YES. One in five enterprises already report that AI operating costs including tokens limit their use (McKinsey, first fire), and a report that runs three fires a day across a ~130-skill corpus is precisely the workload where unvalidated accumulation goes quadratic. Pair it with ACE: add lessons, delete the failed ones, and validate the compaction rather than trusting it — which is the same discipline as bullet 1(c), applied to memory instead of to skills.

praxis_lesson: THIRD FIRE. The 06:04 fire found that a taxonomy is a filter you cannot see through. The 10:05 fire found the worse version — that this report defers the items it controls in favour of the items it can only comment on. THIS FIRE FINDS THE COST, and it is denominated in the only currency that matters: two items published on the same day, September 1 — one aimed at our agent fleet (AIR, skill vetting, $50M, 27% filtered) and one inside our own trade (Yodeck's MCP agent for signage) — sat unread for EIGHT DAYS while five consecutive leads were commentary on a company we do not work with, cannot influence and do not buy from. Nothing was hidden. Both were on the first page of an obvious search. What failed was not the sweep's sources but its SHAPE: a daily recency rank surfaces whatever the industry press is loudest about today and will never surface a week-old item that matters more, because NEW and RELEVANT are different orderings and this report implements only one of them. So the rule the second fire could not quite reach: RECENCY IS A SORT, NOT A FILTER — a scan that only sorts will miss anything that was true yesterday. The correction is one cheap addition and it should be built before another word of commentary is written: a WEEKLY ENUMERATION over the two trades we actually earn money in, signage and AI-operator work, asking 'what shipped in this vertical in the last 30 days,' ignoring recency entirely, and read against what we have already carried. That is the machinery for coverage the 10:05 fire said the format lacks; it is a search, not a system. Second, and this is the sentence to keep: on Sep 1 the market funded skill-vetting at $50M and a signage vendor shipped the agent layer for our clients' screens; on Sep 4 Anthropic handed us a free skill diagnostic; on Sep 5, 7 and 8 this report wrote about OpenAI's disclosure taxonomy and did not run the diagnostic. THE REPORT IS NOW THE SECOND-BEST DOCUMENTED EXAMPLE IN ITS OWN PAGES OF THE FAILURE IT KEEPS DIAGNOSING IN OTHERS — the first being a company whose incident log we do not have, while our own is still not opened. Standing actions, unchanged and now first rather than last: open the misalignment incident log; copy Entra's four MCP controls into a config script; RUN /skill-doctor against the ~130-skill corpus; watch MCP Live! tomorrow, which is the only one of the four that expires.
